blurb: British woodcock-hunting spaniel, now split into English and American breeds
description: The Cocker Spaniel is a medium-small gun dog of British origin, bred to flush woodcock, now two breeds, English and American, with long ears and a silky coat.
answer: Cocker Spaniel is the name for two related spaniel breeds, the English Cocker Spaniel and the smaller American Cocker Spaniel. Both descend from British gun dogs bred to flush and retrieve woodcock, and they stand roughly 34–41 cm depending on breed and sex.

body: Spaniels are mentioned in fourteenth-century writings and were assumed to come from Spain. By 1801 the land spaniel was divided into springers and cockers, the name coming from woodcock hunting. Until about 1900 a cocker was simply a spaniel under 25 lb (11 kg); the Kennel Club separated English Cockers from English Springers in 1892.

Ch. Obo, born in 1879, is seen as the father of the English Cocker, and his American-born son Obo II as the progenitor of the American Cocker. The AKC recognised the English Cocker separately in 1946, and the UK recognised the American in 1970. The American Cocker was the most popular dog in the US for many years.

The American Cocker is smaller with a shorter back, domed head and shorter muzzle: 34–39 cm and about 11–14 kg. The English Cocker is taller with a narrower head and chest: 38–41 cm and 13–15 kg for show dogs. Coats come in black, liver, red and golden solids, black and tan, roans, tricolors and parti-colors. UK working-strain English Cockers are leaner, with shorter ears and less feathering.

Both breeds were developed as gun dogs that quarter close to the handler and retrieve with a soft mouth. English Cockers are commonly described as friendly and affectionate; working-strain dogs are noted for high stamina and drive and can be demanding as pets without training and mental stimulation.

Show-type Cockers have longer ears and a thicker, silkier coat with heavy feathering, which generally needs regular grooming; working strains have shorter, finer coats needing less upkeep. Sources give little detail on exercise, but as gun dogs both breeds are usually considered active.

Sources state that the two breeds share similar health issues with a few exceptions but do not name specific conditions. Breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: What is the difference between English and American Cocker Spaniels?
faq.a: The American Cocker is smaller, with a shorter back, domed head and shorter muzzle; the English Cocker is taller with a narrower head and chest.

faq.q: How big does a Cocker Spaniel get?
faq.a: American Cockers stand about 34–39 cm and weigh 11–14 kg; English Cockers stand about 38–41 cm and show dogs weigh 13–15 kg.

faq.q: Why is it called a Cocker Spaniel?
faq.a: The name comes from the dog's use in hunting woodcock.
